transcript:
This is NPR News Now.
The latest headlines every hour.
Live from NPR News in Washington, I'm Corva Coleman.
The French prime minister has announced that partial curfews may be imposed in some French
towns starting this evening.
That follows the weekend's violence and destruction.
NPR's Eleanor Beardsley reports the measure could inflame people, but the government is
under pressure to stop violence.
Roving bands of youths rioted in towns across France over the weekend.
Twenty-three-year-old Lena Pavay is looking at a looted store with broken windows in Paris.
I understand people are very angry and everything.
I just don't understand why they would attack small shops.
Small shopkeepers have the same worries as the protesters, she says.
In a speech Sunday night, President Macron condemned the violence, but said the troublemaker
should not be confused with protesters with legitimate demands.
The student protest movement has now been joined by public-sector workers and the white working-class
protesters who dogged Macron during his first term, known as the Yellow Vests.
They are calling for another round of protests Saturday.
Eleanor Beardsley in Pierre News, Paris.
Iran has intensified its strikes on commercial vessels transiting through the Strait of Hormuz.
Maritime monitoring shows October has seen the highest number of shipping attacks since
the early days of the Iran war.
And Pierre's Hadil El-Shalci has more.
The UK Maritime Trade Operations, or UKMTO, which is run by the British Navy, said it
logged 10 attacks in the Strait of Hormuz last week alone, including one that sank a
ship.
The monitoring group said it was "struggling" to accurately report the true number of attacks
because the majority of vessels are refusing to report them.
It said that the recent surge is mostly concentrated off the coast of Oman.
Iran increased its strikes on shipping vessels in the Strait of Hormuz as the U.S. tightens
its economic blockade on the country.
But oil exports have rebounded to near pre-war levels as the U.S. Navy escorts vessels through
the critical waterway.
Hadil El-Shalci, NPR News, Istanbul.
President Trump will travel to central Kansas today for a campaign rally to support Republican
Senator Roger Marshall.
From member station KMUW, Mag.
Britain Melis reports the Senate race has become a surprising toss-up.
The president is set to headline a rally at the 6,500-seat Hartling Credit Union Arena
just north of Wichita.
Trump announced the Kansas stop last week as polls showed Republican Senator Roger Marshall
tied or falling slightly behind his Democratic challenger Adam Hamilton, a Methodist pastor.
Both parties have redirected tens of millions of dollars in recent weeks to try and shape
the race.
Kansas voters have not elected a Democrat to the Senate since 1932.
Marshall is an avid supporter of the Trump administration and has defended its handling
of tariffs in the war in Iran.
For NPR News, I'm Meg Britton-Melis in Wichita, Kansas.
And you're listening to NPR News.
President Trump says his planned renovations to a Washington, D.C. golf course will begin
immediately.
Writing online this morning, Trump dismissed opponents who have filed suit to stop him.
A federal judge has ordered a halt to any renovation work until the lawsuit is heard.
Teenagers who become addicted to social media are more likely to develop symptoms of depression.
Teens with depression are also more likely to become addicted to social media.
NPR's Ritu Chatterjee reports on a new study published in the journal Pediatrics.
The findings come from analyzing data on more than 11,000 teenagers.
Researchers followed these teens over five years as part of the adolescent brain and
cognitive development study.
They assess the teenager's mental health annually using standardized questionnaires
on symptoms of anxiety and depression.
And they assess them for symptoms of social media addiction.
Pediatrician Dr. Jason Nagata is at the University of California San Francisco and an author
of the new study.
Social media use and depression can create a vicious cycle for some teenagers where they
kind of reinforce one another and can exacerbate each other's symptoms.
The study did not find a similar relationship between social media addiction and anxiety.
Ritu Chatterjee, NPR News.
What's known as the "leap second" is going to be canceled.
The international authority responsible for timekeeping has been adding a leap second
from time to time, just like a leap year is held every four years.
Instead, scientists will wait for the right time to add a leap hour, but they say that
might not happen for centuries.
You're listening to NPR.

topics.text: French prime minister says partial curfews may be imposed in some towns after weekend riots
Eleanor Beardsley reports on youth riots and looting across France, and Macron's condemnation
Iran intensifies strikes on commercial vessels in the Strait of Hormuz, October highest attack count
UKMTO reports 10 Strait of Hormuz attacks last week, one sinking a ship, under-reporting concerns
President Trump to campaign in Kansas for Senator Roger Marshall in tight Senate race
Trump says renovations to Washington, D.C. golf course will begin immediately despite federal court halt
Study finds teens addicted to social media are more likely to develop depression symptoms
International timekeeping authority cancels the leap second, plans future leap hour instead
